objects.name: Mandiant M-Trends 2026
objects.description: STIX 2.1 bundle transcoded from curated CTI for vendor Mandiant/Google.

objects.name: Landscape
objects.description: In 2025, Mandiant observed a clear divergence in adversary pacing. Cyber criminal groups optimized for immediate impact and deliberate recovery denial. Sophisticated cyber espionage groups and insider threats optimized for extreme persistence, utilizing unmonitored edge devices and native network functionalities to evade detection. Grounded in over 500,000 hours of frontline incident investigations conducted by Mandiant globally in 2025.

objects.name: Initial Vectors
objects.description: Exploitation of internet-facing systems remained the leading initial infection vector for the sixth consecutive year, accounting for 32% of cases. Voice phishing climbed to the second-most common initial infection vector at 11%, displacing traditional email phishing which fell to just 6% — less than half its share the prior year.

objects.name: Breakout Handoff
objects.description: Access-broker handoffs measured in 22 seconds. A growing share of Mandiant investigations followed a division-of-labor model in which one threat cluster gains initial access and transfers it to a separate group for follow-on operations. This pattern appeared in 9% of 2025 investigations, up from 4% in 2022.

objects.name: Unc6201
objects.description: Threat cluster UNC6201 deliberately targets edge and core network devices — VPNs and routers — that typically lack standard EDR telemetry. Mandiant investigated incidents where UNC6201 deployed the BRICKSTORM backdoor on Linux- and BSD-based appliances from multiple manufacturers. Using valid credentials likely captured on the network device, UNC6201 accessed VMware vCenter servers and ESXi hosts. With access to vCenter, the cluster cloned virtual machines including SSO identity providers, secret vaults, and domain controllers. BRICKSTORM achieved dwell times of nearly 400 days.

objects.name: Unc6040
objects.description: In first half of 2025, UNC6040 used voice phishing to convince targets to hand over credentials and authorize attacker-controlled versions of legitimate SaaS applications. Victims later received ShinyHunters-branded extortion notes. Threat actors bypass standard defenses by harvesting long-lived OAuth tokens and session cookies.

objects.name: Unc3944
objects.description: UNC3944, a financially motivated cluster with overlap with publicly reported Scattered Spider activity, continued targeting help desk staff by impersonating employees requesting password resets and multi-factor authentication changes.

objects.name: PROMPTFLUX
objects.description: PROMPTFLUX: experimental VBScript dropper first identified by GTIG in June 2025. Uses the Gemini API to rewrite its own source code on an hourly basis, generating fresh malicious code on demand that evades signature-based detection. First observed instance of 'just-in-time' AI integration in malicious software. Still in testing phases and not yet capable of widespread compromise.

x_cti_metadata.ai_integration: Gemini API for hourly code rewrite

objects.name: PROMPTSTEAL
objects.description: PROMPTSTEAL: attributed to Russian government-backed actor APT28 (also tracked as FROZENLAKE). Queries an LLM to generate one-line Windows commands for document theft. Marking the first confirmed attribution of LLM-assisted malware to a nation-state actor.

x_cti_metadata.ai_integration: LLM query for Windows command generation
x_cti_metadata.significance: first LLM-assisted malware attributed to nation-state

objects.name: QUIETVAULT
objects.description: QUIETVAULT credential stealer observed checking targeted machines for local AI command-line tools, executing predefined prompts to search for configuration files.

x_cti_metadata.technique: searches for local AI CLI tools and config files

objects.name: CVE-2025-31324
objects.description: CVE-2025-31324: improper authorization flaw in SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer component allowing unauthenticated file uploads. Multiple threat clusters exploited it as a zero-day before SAP patched it in April 2025. Several suspected PRC-nexus espionage groups exploited it afterward. Post-compromise activity centered on web shell installation and reconnaissance.

objects.name: CVE-2025-61882
objects.description: CVE-2025-61882: improper authentication vulnerability in Oracle E-Business Suite allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. A threat cluster claiming CL0P affiliation sent extortion emails in September 2025. Mandiant identified evidence of successful exploitation as early as August 2025 and attributes the activity to a suspected FIN11 cluster.

objects.name: Malware Stats
objects.description: GTIG began tracking 714 new malware families in 2025, a significant increase from 632 in 2024, bringing the total to over 6,000 tracked families. 224 malware families observed in 2025 investigations (126 newly tracked, 98 from prior years). Most frequently observed roles: backdoors 36%, downloaders 11%, ransomware 10%, droppers 10%, credential stealers 9%.

objects.name: Exploit Timeline
objects.description: M-Trends 2026 reveals that the mean time to exploit vulnerabilities dropped to an estimated -7 days, meaning exploitation is routinely occurring before a patch is even released.

objects.name: Detection Source
objects.description: In 2025, 52% of organizations detected evidence of malicious activity internally (up from 43% in 2024). External entity notifications declined from 43% to 34%. Adversary notification (e.g. ransom note) remained at 14%.

objects.name: Recovery Denial
objects.description: Ransomware operators have moved beyond dual-threat encryption-and-theft toward systematically denying organizations the ability to recover. They target identity services, virtualization management planes, and backup infrastructure. Mandiant investigated breaches where threat actors exploited misconfigured AD CS templates to create admin accounts exempt from MFA. Attackers extracted dozens of high-privilege credentials from enterprise credential vaults, forced password changes on privileged accounts, locked defenders out during crisis. Deployed ransomware at hypervisor level.
